title: Developer Velocity Messaging - Hosted API
content:
Purpose:
Quick, pragmatic messaging + competitive notes to fuel a developer-focused hosted API landing page, hero copy for the Console onboarding flow, and a few pricing-language variants for experiments (email, paid ads, feature page). This is tactical — feel free to rip lines for A/B tests.

Status/context:
- Draft created after product workshop (Oct 2024) and initial customer interviews with two PLG startups and one enterprise platform team.
- Goal: emphasize developer velocity and predictable inference economics rather than raw model access.
- Constraints: keep hosted pricing simple and predictable; direct power users to Dedicated/Private.

Target audience slices (prioritized):
1) Early-stage product engineers & founders — want fastest path from idea -> prototype, low friction SDKs and demos.
2) Platform/infra engineers at scale-ups — care about predictable latency, per-route observability, and rollout controls.
3) Procurement/Security reviewers (secondary) — need clear notes about data handling, SLAs, and contract options.

Key developer-first value props (concise):
- Ship features fast: SDKs (JS/Python), example apps, and one-click console tokens get you from signup to a prototype in < 10 minutes.
- Predictable performance: verified latency profiles, tiered SLAs, and automatic fallbacks keep user-facing flows snappy.
- Cost control without surprises: token-level cost analytics, batching suggestions, and transparent pricing for hosted usage.
- Same API across environments: start on hosted, scale to Dedicated or Private with no SDK/API changes.

Quickstart angles (audience-fit and CTA):
- "Prototype in 10": hero CTA for founders/PMs. Demo: 5-line JS snippet that streams a response and renders partials in the browser.
- "Integrate, then optimize": target infra engineers — show how to toggle batching, enable kv-cache, and view per-route cost.
- "From PoC to SLA": narrative for platform teams about predictable throughput and direct upgrade path to Dedicated capacity.

Sample quickstart (text form for landing page):
- Headline: "Build and ship LLM features in minutes — production economics you can trust."
- Subhead: "Hosted API, predictable latency, and clear cost controls. Same API if you ever want to move on-prem."
- CTA variants: "Start prototyping (free credits)", "See latency & cost benchmarks", "Get a dedicated trial"

Pricing-language drafts (hosted tier experiments):
Variant A — Simple per-token (developer friendly):
- "Pay as you go: $0.0008 / token (generation), $0.0004 / token (input). Free tier: 50k tokens / month for 3 months. No surprises — token usage and per-route cost visible in Console."
Variant B — Predictable dev tier + usage overage:
- "Developer plan: $49/mo (includes 1M tokens). Overage billed at $0.0006/token. Ideal for daily prototyping and small apps."
Variant C — Commitment-first (nudge to Dedicated for enterprise):
- "Hosted for growth. For predictable sustained throughput, consider Redwood Dedicated (reserved capacity, SLA). Contact sales for committed rates and migration assistance."

Notes on language tone and traps to avoid:
- Avoid technical jargon in hero copy (e.g., don’t lead with KV cache or quantization). Reserve those for docs/ops pages.
- Emphasize predictability & observability in page subsections — engineers love instrumentation language (traces, token-level breakdowns).
- Be explicit about migration path: "same API" is a high-value promise — show it visually in docs.

Competitive analysis (short, tactical):
- OpenAI: strong brand & dev mindshare. Strengths: broad ecosystem, rich model family. Weaknesses: perceived lack of deployment flexibility and higher variance in latency for larger prompts. Message: call out Redwood’s predictability and deployment/compliance options.
- Anthropic: safety-first positioning; good for regulated customers. Strengths: model safety. Weaknesses: less focus on cost tooling/ops. Message: highlight Redwood Optimize tooling and cost controls.
- AWS Bedrock / GCP Vertex: attractive to infra teams already committed to cloud provider. Strengths: cloud integration. Weaknesses: vendor lock-in and less model/serving specialization. Message: emphasize multi-environment parity and less friction migrating between hosted/dedicated/private.
- Self-hosted inference (various vendors & OSS stacks): Strengths: full control, potentially lower marginal cost at huge scale. Weaknesses: ops burden, slower iteration. Message: Redwood offers the ops primitives without the maintenance tax — show time-to-first-50k-requests estimate vs self-host.

Competitive messaging hooks for site copy
- "If you care about speed from idea -> product, we’re built for you."
- "Stop guessing about token spend — measure and optimize in the Console."
- "Same API whether you run with us or in your VPC."

Objections and short responses (for sales/ads):
- "We can self-host and save money": response — "Maybe at extreme scale, but you’ll spend months building and maintaining the stack. Redwood reduces time-to-market and provides predictable SLOs out of the box."
- "We need guaranteed SLAs": response — "Hosted provides transparent performance tiers; for contractual SLAs and dedicated throughput we offer Redwood Dedicated."
- "Security / data residency concerns": response — "Private deployment options (VPC/on-prem) with KMS/HSM integrations and audit logs — same API and tooling."

Measurement & success signals for experiments:
- Conversion funnel: visited quickstart -> clicked SDK -> created API key -> first 1000 tokens generated.
- Time-to-first-PR: time from signup to a GitHub commit referencing our SDK snippet.
- Cost-awareness: % of new accounts that enable token-level analytics within 7 days.

Open questions / decisions to make:
- Free tier amount: 25k vs 50k tokens? (ask growth)
- Which pricing variant to A/B first: Variant A or B? Proposal: run A for 4 weeks, measure conversion and NRR.
- Landing page hero CTA: "Start prototyping" vs "See benchmarks" — which performs better for enterprise upsell?

Next steps / TODOs:
- @Priya: draft lightweight benchmarks page with 3 real-world scenarios (chat UI, summarization pipeline, reranking). Linked to GTM-412.
- @Ethan: prepare 2 landing hero art directions (developer-focused vs enterprise-focused) for marketing sync (due 2024-11-18).
- Product: finalize free-tier amount and gating rules (internal ticket: PRODHQ-223).

Appendix: quick copy snippets for testing
- Short ad headline: "Build smarter apps faster — predictable inference, zero ops."
- Email subject: "Prototype an LLM feature in 10 minutes — free credits inside"
- Slack microcopy (Console): "Need more throughput? Try Dedicated trials — we'll help with migration."
